meta.title: Imambargahs / Karbalas of Pakistan - historic and notable sites by city
notes: Built from public news and heritage sources. NOT a complete list: Peshawar alone is reported to have 93 imambargahs (63 operational) and Quetta about 56, but only a few are named in sources.
latitude/longitude are null unless a map listing showed them (marked approximate in notes). Use google_maps_url (Google Maps search link) or geocode the address.
contact: phone numbers come from Waze map listings and are NOT verified; call before publishing. Most entries have no published phone.
year_built is as stated by the source; several dates are traditions or disputed and are marked in notes.

verified = false means not confirmed by phone or visit. 'confidence' says how well the entry is backed: 'news/heritage source', 'map listing', 'social page title only', or 'unconfirmed (Gemini list only)'.
The Lahore entries LHR-IB-010 to LHR-IB-018 were added after the user shared a Gemini list; entries marked 'unconfirmed (Gemini list only)' had no independent source in my searches.
Facebook pages for Jamia Ali Masjid and Jageer Ali Akbar could not be opened (blocked to automated readers), so details from them are missing.
No imambargahs could be named for Multan or Faisalabad from the sources I could open; Multan's Muharram processions run between shrines (Shah Yousaf Gardez to Shah Shams Sabzwari).

points.name: Karbala Gamay Shah
points.founder_or_caretaker: Qizilbash family built it around the burial of Baba Syed Ghulam Ali Shah (Gamay Shah); manager Shabab Hussain Zaidi (2010)
points.notes: Contains the grave of Baba Gamay Shah and a zarih of Imam Hussain. The Muharram 10 procession ends here; processions are said to date back over 200 years. Sources date Gamay Shah to the 'early 18th century' but link him to Ranjit Singh (1799-1839), so the saint's dates are inconsistent.

points.name: Mubarak Haveli
points.area: Mohallah Shia'an Kashmirian near Mochi Gate (a reader comment says inside Bhati Gate)
points.founder_or_caretaker: Built by Nawab Ali Raza; cared for by his great-grandson Mansoor Ali Qazalbash
points.notes: Large green wooden gate and courtyard. Location is disputed in reader comments, so confirm on site.

points.name: Nisar Haveli
points.address: Mochi Gate area, Walled City, Lahore
points.founder_or_caretaker: Named after Nawab Nisar Ali Khan (great-grandfather of the current organiser)
points.notes: The central Muharram 9 procession departs from here. Has a wooden pulpit and silver and gold-coated alams.

points.name: Maatam Siraai Imambargah
points.year_built: About 500 years ago (claim; described as Lahore's oldest)
points.founder_or_caretaker: Custodian Jafar Ali Shah, descendant of Syeds from Kashmir
points.notes: Named for Shia devotees who stayed here on their way from Kashmir to Najaf. Age is a local claim.

points.name: Chihl Bibian Imambargah
points.area: Mohallah Chihl Bibian, Mochi Gate area
points.address: Mohallah Chihl Bibian, Mochi Gate, Lahore
points.year_built: Not stated (walled graveyard dates to after 1587)
points.founder_or_caretaker: Inside an old haveli of the family of Syed Ahmed Tokhta Tirmizi
points.notes: The Zuljanah procession stops here for a long time. Graves were later declared an imambargah. Link to Sayyeda Ruqayyah is local belief and unverified.

points.name: Imam Bargah Atiya Ahlaibait
points.address: Nicholson Road, Lahore (no street number published)
points.founder_or_caretaker: Founded by Dr. Syed Riaz Ali Shah; speaker Moulana Syed Absar Ali Naqvi
points.notes: Ashra-e-Majalis 1-10 Muharram (6th and 9th especially important); monthly majlis on the first Sunday of each Islamic month, 4pm to before Maghrib; ladies majlis after Zohrain on the last Sunday of Muharram. Site says it is one of the oldest in Pakistan; recordings from 1969 to 2024 are online.

points.name: Imambargah Syed Wajid Ali Shah
points.notes: Named only as a stop passed by the procession.

points.name: Imambargah Maulvi Feroz Ali
points.notes: Named only as a stop passed by the procession.

points.name: Imambargah Syed Rajab Ali Shah
points.notes: Named only as a stop passed by the procession.

points.name: Imam Bargah Gulistan-e-Zahra
points.area: Abbott Road / Montgomery Park, Qila Gujjar Singh
points.address: 26 Abbott Road, Montgomery Park, Qila Gujjar Singh, Lahore 54000
points.notes: Probably the 'Gulshan-e-Zahra' you remembered; the real name looks like Gulistan-e-Zahra. Has Facebook, Instagram and YouTube pages named Gulistaan-e-Zehra. Not far from the Bahria Dastarkhwan on Abbot Road.

points.name: Imam Bargah (name not listed), Block H-3, Plot 301
points.address: Plot 301, Block H-3, Phase 2, Johar Town, Lahore
points.notes: Matches the first address in your Gemini list, but Gemini's text did not include the imambargah's name. Yandex Maps lists it only as 'Imam Bargah' (mosque). Coordinates are approximate, read from the Yandex Maps link. 'Near Expo Centre Road' from Gemini is unconfirmed.

points.name: Jamia Ali Masjid & Imambargah
points.address: Main Boulevard, Wafaqi Colony, Johar Town, Lahore (street address from Gemini, unconfirmed)
points.notes: A Facebook page titled 'Jamia Ali Masjid Imam bargha Wafaqi Colony Lahore' exists, which supports the name and area. I could not open it, so address, phone and history are unconfirmed.

points.name: Imambargah Jageer Ali Akbar (A.S)
points.area: Nargis Block, Sector C, Bahria Town
points.address: 271, Hussain Block, Sector C, Nargis Block, Bahria Town, Lahore
points.notes: Also called 'Masjid o Imam Bargah Jageer Shahzada Ali Akbar'. Has Instagram, Facebook and YouTube pages. Matches the Bahria Town entry in your Gemini list and its Nargis Block, Sector C address.

points.name: Imambargah Lalpul
points.address: Nabi Pura, Lahore (no street address given)
points.notes: Found on Yandex Maps, not in your Gemini list. Coordinates are approximate, read from the Yandex link.

points.name: Imam Bargah Qasr-e-Batool (s.a)
points.address: Iqbal Town, Lahore (no street address found)
points.notes: Found while searching for Qasr-e-Sajjad. This is a different imambargah.

points.name: Imambargah Qasr-e-Sajjad
points.address: Main Boulevard DHA, Sector G / Phase 1, DHA, Lahore (from Gemini, unconfirmed)
points.notes: I found no independent source for this name or address. It may exist; confirm on a map before listing.

points.name: Imambargah Model Town
points.address: Block C / Block J, Model Town, Lahore (from Gemini, unconfirmed; two blocks given)
points.notes: I found no independent source. Gemini gave two possible blocks, so the exact one is unknown.

points.name: Imambargah Sarwar Road
points.address: Sarwar Road, Lahore Cantt, Lahore (from Gemini, unconfirmed)
points.notes: I found no independent source; searches returned only property listings for Sarwar Road.

points.name: Imambargah Siraj (Shiraz)
points.year_built: c. 1775 (called the city's oldest by Dr Aqeel Abbas Jaffery)
points.founder_or_caretaker: Originally the Sindhi Shia Siraji community of Moosa Lane
points.notes: Sindhi plate reads 'Imam Warah Siraz'; later name likely refers to Shiraz, Iran.

points.name: Ghareebul Ghurba Imambargah
points.founder_or_caretaker: Fatima 'Phappan', a Khoja Shia Asna Ashri
points.notes: Originally called 'Phappan Ka Pirr'.

points.name: Bishu Imambargah
points.founder_or_caretaker: Founded by trader Bishu
points.notes: Began as one room; later a double-storey stone building. Long a hub of majalis and community life.

points.name: Imambargah Barah Imam
points.founder_or_caretaker: Built by Chaudhary Allah Ditta
points.notes: A composite of five smaller imambargahs (another tradition says twelve). Processions join the main juloos at Denso Hall.

points.name: Barra Imambargah
points.notes: Major pre-Partition site with annual Muharram rituals including alam ceremonies and traditional drumming.

points.name: Imambargah Hussainia Iranian
points.year_built: 1948 (acquired by an Iranian immigrant organisation); became an imambargah after 1960
points.founder_or_caretaker: Iranian immigrant organisation
points.notes: Formerly a pre-Partition community centre. The main Muharram procession culminates here.

points.name: Imambargah Mehfil-i-Shah-i-Khorasan
points.address: Soldier Bazaar, Catholic Colony No. 1, Karachi
points.founder_or_caretaker: Land allotted by Quaid-i-Azam; designed by Muhammad Ali Habib; built for the Habib and Gokal families
points.notes: Known for major Muharram majalis.

points.name: Qaimia Imambargah
points.founder_or_caretaker: Syed Abu Jafar Zaidi, a migrant from Awadh
points.notes: Named after his ancestral imambargah in Safipur. Faced a contested property claim.

points.name: Imambargah Shah Wilayat
points.founder_or_caretaker: Syed Istijab Hassan Naqvi, an Amroha migrant
points.notes: Redeveloped over time; includes zarih replicas.

points.name: Imambargah Jaffar-i-Tayyar
points.founder_or_caretaker: Volunteers led by Ali Hasan Zaidi ('Darogha Ji')
points.notes: Construction was repeatedly disrupted; volunteers held nightly vigils on site.

points.name: Shah-i-Karbala Trust (Rizvia) Imambargah
points.founder_or_caretaker: Part of a settlement envisioned in 1948 by Maulana Aneesul Hasnain and Advocate Qazalbash, mostly for Lucknow-origin migrants

points.name: Qadeemi Imambargah (Imamkot)
points.founder_or_caretaker: Agha Mustafa Shah and Agha Fazal Ali Shah; managed by Anjuman Imamia Asna Ashria
points.notes: Originally had Kashmiri-style wooden balconies; fire damage in 1966, later rebuilt. All mourning processions end here.

points.name: Colonel Maqbool Hussain Imambargah
points.founder_or_caretaker: Colonel Maqbool Hussain converted a large haveli
points.notes: The central Muharram 10 procession has started here since November 1947. Three-storey building with wooden balconies and coloured glass.

points.name: Hifazat Ali Shah Imambargah
points.year_built: Pre-Partition (family held a procession licence dated 1887)
points.founder_or_caretaker: Founded by the grandfather of the present family, who came from Gali Syedan, Delhi; custodian Iqrar Hussain
points.notes: Over 18 marlas; holds 3,000+ people; processions leave on Muharram 7 and 10. Custodian claims it is the garrison city's oldest.

points.name: Ashiq Hussain Imambargah
points.notes: A main Ashura procession starts here and joins others on Iqbal Road.

points.name: Imambargah Kashmirian
points.notes: Zuljinnah processions join the main Ashura procession at Raja Bazaar and Purana Qila.

points.name: Markazi Imambargah G-6/2
points.founder_or_caretaker: Anjuman Saadat-i-Amroha and Khawaja Murtaza (procession)
points.notes: The main Muharram 9 procession starts here and circles the sector.

points.name: Imambargah Agha Syed Alam Shah Awal
points.year_built: First Zuljinah procession reportedly began here in 1890
points.notes: Source is a book by Mukhtar Ali Nayyar cited by Dawn.

points.name: Imambargah Sain Zareen
points.notes: The main procession starts here at 4pm on Muharram 9 and returns on Muharram 10.

points.name: Babul Hawaij Imambargah
points.notes: Described as the oldest in Peshawar. The article says Peshawar has 93 imambargahs, 63 still operational.

points.name: Imambargah Kalan
points.year_built: Not stated (described as the first imambargah in the main city)
points.notes: Sheltered earthquake victims in May 1935. A Hazara imambargah on this road was attacked on 4 July 2003. The name-to-road match comes from a search result title, so confirm it.

points.name: Punjabi Imambargah
points.area: Starting point of the main Muharram procession
points.notes: Route runs via Alamdar Road.

points.name: Imambargah Nasir-ul-Aza
points.notes: The main procession ends here, together with Imambargah Kalan. Quetta reportedly has about 56 imambargahs.

points.name: Karbala Dadan Shah
points.area: End of the Ashura procession route
points.notes: The Ashura procession ends here at around 4am.

points.name: Qadam Gah Maula Ali
points.notes: The central Ashura procession starts here at 10am. This is a Muharram shrine site, not an imambargah.
